X.|OF THE APOSTLES.|317}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=9|verse=36}}† And in Ioppé there vvas a certaine disciple named Tabitha, vvhich by interpretation is called Dorcas. This vvoman vvas ful of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Behold good vvorkes and almes-deedes, & the force thereof reaching euen to the next life.}}∷ good vvorkes and almes-deedes vvhich she did. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=37}}† And it came to passe in those daies, that she vvas sicke and died. Vvhom vvhen they had vvashed, they laid her in an vpper chamber. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=38}}† And vvhereas Lydda vvas nigh to Ioppé, the disciples hearing that Peter vvas in it, they sent tvvo men vnto him, desiring him, Be not loth to come so farre as to vs. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=39}}† And Peter rising vp came vvith them. And vvhen he vvas come, they brought him into the vpper chamber: and al the vvidovves stoode about him vveeping, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The praiers of our Almes folke & beadsmen may do vs great good euen after our departure. For if they procured her temporal life, much more may they helpe vs to Gods mercie and to release of punishment in Purgatorie.}}∷ and shevving him the coates and garments vvhich Dorcas made them. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=40}}† And al being put forth, Peter falling on his knees praied, and turning to the body he said: Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eies: and seeing Peter, she sate vp.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=41}}† And giuing her his hand, he lifted her vp. And vvhen he had called the saincts and the vvidovves, he presented her aliue. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=42}}† And it vvas made knovven through out al Ioppé: and many beleeued in our Lord. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=43}}† And it came to passe that he abode many daies in Ioppé, vvith one Simon a tanner.

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The}} 4. part.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. X.}}}}}}

{{c|''Because the Ievves so much abhorred the Gentils, for the better vvarrant of their Christening, an Angel appeareth to Cornelius the deuout Italian. 9 and a vision is shevved to Peter him self ( the cheefe and Pastor of al) 19 and the Spirit speaketh to him, 34 yea and as he is Catechizing them about IESVS, 44 the holy Ghost commeth visibly vpon them: and therfore not fearing any longer the offense of the Ievves, he commaundeth to baptize them.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=10|verse=1}}}}ND there vvas a certaine man in Cæsaréa, named Cornelius, Centurion of that vvhich is called the Italian band, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=2}}† religious, & fearing God vvith al his house, {{sup|‖}} doing many almes-deedes to the people. And alvvaies praying to God, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=3}}† he savv in a vision manifestly, about the ninthe houre of the day, an Angel of God comming in vnto him, and saying to him, Cornelius. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=4}}† But he beholding him, taken vvith feare, said, Vvho art thou Lord? And he said to him, Thy praiers and thy almes-deedes are ascended into remembrance in the sight of God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=5}}† And novv send men<noinclude>{{rh||Rr iij|vnto}}</noinclude>
